pages: Day 124: We burn the houses now. He says the sickness sits in the wood the way it sits in the flesh, and I believe Him, because the fire does not go out. Three days after we leave, the beams still glow under the ash. Touch them and they bite.

The men pile the bones outside the walls where the road comes in, so the next village sees what we are before we arrive. He does not stop them. He says fear keeps the healthy indoors and the sick in their beds, and that is where we find them.
I write the names of the villages in the back of this book. I no longer write the names of the people. There is not enough paper.
